s own `🧫️fixtures/`, and the envelope region of `🧰️framework/🛍️products/💻️os/🔨️modules/🧬️semio/🦀️.rs`. It imports nothing from and transliterates nothing of the Rust it judges, and it needs no host package, which is why `package` is empty. The protocol description stops at the repeated `nodes`/`edges` records and names only their shape; that shape was turned into a reader and a writer by taking the field order from the DSL grammar, and the derivation is PINNED by the implementation re-encoding the committed `../../✉️base/📚️examples/🌊️pipeline/🖼️assets/🎒️.pack.semio` byte for byte. The earlier `semio-flow-mutation-semantics` no-oracle decision this entry replaces declined json-rust as a weak reference — a generic JSON DOM supplies no knowledge of nodes, edges, ports or params, so every one of the thirteen semantics would still have been hand-written on top of it. That judgement stands; what changed is that a second implementation of the VOCABULARY now exists, in another language, and the two are compared scenario for scenario. The artifact the case mutates is likewise real rather than synthetic: a 180-node, 179-edge connection network derived once from the committed Nakagin Capsule Tower IFC 4 model with IfcOpenShell 0.8.4.\n\nUNDER PROTOCOL V2 this registration is classified `cross-semio-implementation` — a required SUPPLEMENTAL oracle that does not discharge `semio-v1-flow-mutate`
